tonight.headline: Claims lock at 01:00 tonight. Everything else in this brief can wait; that cannot.
body: Week 2 has not kicked off. ESPN has Panda Attack 125.4 to your 121.6 and gives you 48%. Nothing on either roster is locked, so this is a projection and not a position.

Your one hard deadline is the waiver run at 01:00 Wednesday, Mexico City. Three claims are below, in the order to place them. The Wednesday-morning brief lands after they have already processed, so whatever you want claimed has to be in the queue before you sleep. The flex swap you made at 17:58 today is done and is not repeated here.

case.label: What decides it
case.body: Panda Attack reset their lineup at 15:25 today and start Dak Prescott over Jalen Hurts, with Jaylen Waddle, Harold Fannin Jr. and Jordan Mason on their bench. Their 125.4 is a full lineup with no injury holes in it. You do not beat that number tonight; you beat it on Sunday with a better kicker and, if the claim lands, a fourth startable receiver.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Anything that moves either projection materially before Sunday — a Panda Attack starter ruled out, or Coker landing and starting for you. Neither is knowable tonight.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Waivers clear 01:00 Wednesday, Mexico City · place this claim FIRST
doFirst.title: Claim Jalen Coker, drop Matthew Stafford
doFirst.subtitle: Last brief before claims lock. Nothing has moved the ankle read since Monday, and Carolina's first practice is Wednesday — after the claim runs.

case.label: The player
case.body: 8 catches on 9 targets for 138 yards and two touchdowns in Week 1, most of it after he rolled the ankle in the first quarter. 51.0% rostered nationally and free in a ten-team league is the ownership-anomaly band the strategy file calls the strongest single wire signal.

case.label: The ankle, re-checked at 16:00
case.body: Nothing new since Monday. Coker was photographed in a boot at practice on 14 September, called it precautionary — 'just rolled my ankle a little bit' — said he does not expect to miss time and expects to practise Wednesday. DraftKings Network, NBC, Yahoo and Heavy all carry the same account and none of them has updated it today. ESPN still lists him QUESTIONABLE.

case.label: The clock problem you cannot solve
case.body: Carolina's first Week 2 practice report lands Wednesday. The claim processes at 07:00 UTC Wednesday, which is 01:00 Wednesday where you are — hours before the report exists. You are claiming blind and that is accepted on purpose, because Chem priority resets weekly and a lost claim costs nothing lasting. This is the whole reason the Tuesday-evening run exists.

case.label: The drop, on the record
case.body: Stafford is 92.5% rostered and this disagrees with the market deliberately. Chem starts one quarterback, Josh Allen is QB1 on Yahoo's Week 2 board, and the Chem wire currently holds Brock Purdy, Bo Nix and Baker Mayfield as waiver claims if Allen ever needs covering. A backup quarterback in a one-QB ten-team league is the cheapest seat on this roster.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Coker is limited or absent in Carolina's Wednesday practice report, or carries a designation into Sunday; or Tetairoa McMillan reasserts as the clear No. 1 and Coker's target share falls under about 18% across Weeks 2–3.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Waivers clear 01:00 Wednesday, Mexico City · place this claim SECOND
doFirst.title: Claim Tyler Loop, drop Chris Boswell
doFirst.subtitle: K4 against K17 on this week's board, and the churn argument that blocked this yesterday was imported from the other league.

case.label: The gap
case.body: Yahoo's Week 2 kicker board has Tyler Loop 4th and Chris Boswell 17th. Loop's Week 1 'went a long way toward quieting' the accuracy questions he carried into the season — multiple long field goals — and Baltimore host New Orleans, the highest-scoring environment available to any kicker on this wire. Boswell goes to New England in a game nobody has priced as a shootout.

case.label: Why this was blocked yesterday and is not today
case.body: The standing hold on Boswell says Eddy Pineiro 'was dropped FOR Boswell on 8 September, six days ago' and that reversing a kicker slot inside a week is the churn pattern the log already carries twice. That transaction is in the IPADE log, not this one. Chem's activity feed contains no kicker move at all in its visible window, and the twin CHURN entries are both IPADE's Little–Boswell reversal. The Chem kicker seat has not changed hands, so the seven-day rule does not close it.

case.label: Honest size
case.body: This is a kicker. ESPN's own weekly numbers put it at less than a point (8.5 to 7.6) and the season field at 3.8. The ranking gap is thirteen places and the claim is free, which is why it is worth queuing — not because it is large. Place it behind Coker: if Coker is awarded, this one may fail, and that is an acceptable outcome.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Chem's activity log turns out to contain a Boswell add on 8 September that is simply outside the visible window — the feed only reaches back to 09 September, so this cannot be proved from the file, only that the identical transaction is visible in IPADE. Also falsified if Baltimore's implied total falls below 22 or Loop misses twice in Week 2.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Waivers clear 01:00 Wednesday, Mexico City · place this claim THIRD, or skip it
doFirst.title: Claim the Ravens defense, drop the Jaguars defense
doFirst.subtitle: Downgraded again. Two Week 2 boards now have Jacksonville close to Baltimore, and one of them has Jacksonville ahead.

case.label: Why Baltimore still leads
case.body: Every Week 2 board puts Baltimore in the top six. Draft Sharks has them 4th at 8.4 projected; Sportsnaut has them 4th overall and 6th for fantasy, on a Week 1 in which a defense under new coordinator Jesse Minter sacked Daniel Jones twice, forced an interception and held Indianapolis to 149 net passing yards. They are 89.8% rostered nationally and sitting free here.

case.label: Why the case keeps shrinking
case.body: This started Monday on Lindy's having Baltimore 2nd and Jacksonville 9th. NBC put them in the same tier yesterday afternoon. Today Draft Sharks has Jacksonville 18th — and Sportsnaut has Jacksonville 3rd overall and 8th for Week 2, two places behind Baltimore, after five sacks, two takeaways and one-of-eight on third down against Cleveland. Two boards say big gap, two say almost none. That is a split, not a consensus.

case.label: The premise that broke
case.body: The whole Baltimore case rested on Jacksonville drawing a hard road game at Denver. Sportsnaut's Week 1 review has Denver missing 28 tackles on Monday night and allowing 247 yards after a missed tackle, and reads Jacksonville at Denver as a strong defensive spot rather than a bad one. The reason to move off Jacksonville is weaker than it was twenty-four hours ago.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Baltimore finish outside the top 12 defenses in Week 2, or Jacksonville finish top 5 at Denver. Either says a one-week board moved this roster for nothing, and this would be the second reversal of the same seat inside three days.

whatWentWrong.title: The JuiceJam offer was built on the wrong read of McLaurin, and it is off the action list
whatWentWrong.lead: He led every Commanders receiver in route participation. The four targets were coverage, not decline — and the offer sold him at the bottom of that.

case.label: What today's data says
case.body: Draft Sharks' Week 1 review has McLaurin at 92.1% route participation, 35 routes, the highest on Washington — against Stefon Diggs at 65.8% and rookie Antonio Williams at 60.5%. Quinyon Mitchell and Riq Woolen covered him on 22 of those 35 routes and gave up one target and no catches. Jayden Daniels completed 52.9% of his passes for 164 yards; the whole passing game failed, not the receiver.

case.label: What the morning brief said instead
case.body: That McLaurin drew four targets to Diggs's nine, that rookie Antonio Williams matched him, and that 'the target split says the room is shared.' Target count without route share is the shallow version of that read, and the strategy file's own rule is that target share and route participation are the floor while touchdowns and single-game target counts are the noise.

case.label: Why it matters tonight
case.body: Washington's coordinator David Blough has said on the record the offense is built around getting McLaurin ten targets a game, and Dallas are without safety Malik Hooker and linebacker DeMarvion Overshown this week. Selling a 92.1%-route-share receiver into that, at the one week his price is lowest, is the 'sell low on usage' mistake the strategy file names explicitly.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: McLaurin draws fewer than six targets against a Dallas secondary missing its starting safety, or his route share drops under 80% while Diggs's climbs. Either would say the Week 1 route count was the anomaly and the sale was right.

whatWentWrong.sources: Draft Sharks · Sports Illustrated / Commanders Daily

whatWentWrong.title: The Boswell hold quoted a transaction from the other league
whatWentWrong.lead: 'Pineiro was dropped FOR Boswell on 8 September' is IPADE's log. Chem's kicker seat has not changed hands.

case.label: The two logs
case.body: IPADE's activity feed shows DROP Cam Little / ADD Chris Boswell at 08 Sep 18:41 and the reverse at 10 Sep 16:17 — the pair of moves the decision log carries twice as CHURN. Chem's feed, visible from 09 September, contains exactly four non-lineup moves and none of them is a kicker.

case.label: Why this is the named failure mode
case.body: VALIDATORS.md lists 'wrong league's projection' as a judgement error no script catches, from the run that quoted Mark Andrews's IPADE number inside a Chem card. This is the same error wearing a transaction instead of a projection, and it blocked a free upgrade for a day.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Chem's activity feed only reaches back to 09 September 03:45, so a Chem kicker move on 8 September cannot be ruled out from the file. If one existed it would now be eight days old anyway, and the seven-day window would be closed either way.

case.label: Where it stands
case.body: Sent 14 September, unanswered through three runs. It recomputes on tonight's file to exactly the same numbers as this morning and as Sunday — 2070.3 to 2092.1 for you, 1966.4 to 1970.2 for them. It is no longer a Do-first card and it is no longer recommended tonight.

case.label: What changed, and it is not the numbers
case.body: McLaurin's Week 1 route participation is 92.1%, the highest on Washington, and the four targets came against Mitchell and Woolen covering him on 22 of 35 routes. He is the receiver the offense is designed around — coordinator David Blough's stated target is ten a game — at the one week his price is lowest. That is a buy profile, not a sell profile.

case.label: The half that is still right
case.body: Stafford genuinely is dead weight: a backup quarterback in a one-QB ten-team league behind the QB1 on the board. Getting anything for him beats dropping him. But he does not move this deal alone — Stafford-for-Smith straight leaves JuiceJam 5.5 worse and there is no one-for-one on either roster where both sides gain. McLaurin is the only reason it clears, which is the problem.

case.label: The honest risk
case.body: Season projections have not moved across four consecutive snapshots. Both sides of this are priced on a field published before the season and never updated, which is the known limitation the runbook names, and the +21.8 should be read as an argument rather than a measurement.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: McLaurin draws fewer than six targets at Dallas while Diggs clears nine again — then the shared-room read was right and this should be re-sent at the same price. Or JuiceJam accept it unprompted before 01:00, in which case it is still a net gain on the published field and not a disaster; it is simply not the trade to chase.

trades.sources: Draft Sharks · Sports Illustrated / Commanders Daily · ESPN league file
trades.copyText: Hi — open to McLaurin + Stafford for DeVonta Smith? You're starting Goff at 277.8, the lowest season projection of any starting QB in the league, and Stafford is 303.4. DJ Moore slots straight back in at WR for McLaurin, so you upgrade the QB spot and keep a full receiver room. On ESPN's season field it's about +3.8 for you. No rush from my side.

worthALook.name: Jakobi Meyers
worthALook.lead: A listed starting receiver, 79% rostered nationally, and he ran more Week 1 routes than the Jaguars receiver you own.

case.label: The role
case.body: Jacksonville's published depth chart lists three starting receivers — Parker Washington in the slot, Brian Thomas Jr. and Jakobi Meyers — with Travis Hunter as a starting cornerback and only a backup receiver. Liam Coen has confirmed Hunter gets 'a package on offense' and otherwise takes mental reps on defense. There is no fourth mouth in that room.

case.label: The number that argues for him
case.body: NBC's Week 1 review, logged on 15 September, has Meyers at 20 routes against Brian Thomas Jr.'s 14 — Meyers ran the most of any Jacksonville receiver. That is the strongest single fact on this page and it cuts against a player you already own, which is exactly why it is written down rather than left out.

case.label: Why he is only a watch
case.body: Your receiver slots are Jefferson and Garrett Wilson with McLaurin in the flex, and the Coker claim is ahead of him for the same kind of seat. Adding Meyers would mean a drop, and both bench receivers — Thomas added 12 September, Likely 13 September — are inside the seven-day churn window. There is no clean seat for him tonight.

case.label: The awkward part
case.body: He is the direct competitor to a player you already own. One of the three named falsification conditions on the Brian Thomas Jr. thesis is 'Meyers out-targets him in Week 2'. Claiming both sides of that question is not a hedge, it is paying twice.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Meyers out-targets Thomas at Denver, or Thomas is ruled out and reopens the seat. Either makes this a claim rather than a row.

doNotChase.name: Stefon Diggs
doNotChase.lead: Nine targets in Week 1 is the number everyone sees. The route share underneath it is the number that matters.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: 65.8% route participation to McLaurin's 92.1%, and a 44.4% catch rate on those nine targets. Nine targets on two-thirds of the routes in a game where the opposing secondary bracketed the other receiver is a distribution artifact, not a role. Antonio Williams ran 60.5%.

case.label: And you cut him nine days ago
case.body: You dropped Diggs on 12 September for Brian Thomas Jr. Re-adding him now would be the reversal pattern the decision log already carries three times as CHURN, on the strength of one box score.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Diggs's route share climbs past 80% over Weeks 2–3 while McLaurin's falls — that would be a genuine role change rather than a target-count blip, and it would also falsify the reason the JuiceJam offer was withdrawn.

doNotChase.name: Eddy Pineiro
doNotChase.lead: 84.8% rostered and free is a real anomaly. He is still the wrong kicker to claim.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Yahoo's Week 2 board has Pineiro 12th. Tyler Loop is 4th on the same board and is equally free on this wire at 51.7% owned. If you are spending a claim on a kicker — and the card above says you should — it is not this one.

case.label: Why he keeps surfacing
case.body: His 146.8 season projection is the highest of any kicker on this wire, which is why a projection-only screen keeps returning him. The season field has not moved in four snapshots; the weekly board has.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Loop is claimed by someone else tonight, or San Francisco's implied totals stay above Baltimore's for two straight weeks. Then Pineiro is the fallback, not the target.

cannotSee.label: Rival claims are invisible
cannotSee.body: ESPN returns only your own pending claims. Nine other managers can see the same 51%-rostered receiver and you are priority 5 of 10. Ordering the claims is the only lever you have.

cannotSee.label: Season projections have not moved in four snapshots
cannotSee.body: Your optimal season total recomputes to 2070.3 exactly, for the fourth consecutive run, and every trade number on this page reproduces to the decimal. Either the field updates weekly and has not yet, or it is a preseason artifact. Anything priced on it is priced on August's opinion.

cannotSee.label: Seven of fourteen matchup tiles are dashed
cannotSee.body: Dallas, Denver, Detroit, San Francisco and the two Jacksonville tiles were researched today. New England, Chicago, Green Bay, the Rams, Minnesota, Carolina and the Pittsburgh kicker tile were not, and are flagged rather than guessed. A dashed tile is 'not looked at', which is different from average.

cannotSee.label: Atlanta's quarterback is still unanswered
cannotSee.body: Kyle Pitts scored 0.0 in Week 1 on 81% route participation because Atlanta were down to a third-string starter. No search this run produced a named Week 2 starter for Atlanta. He stays benched on that absence, not on a read.

cannotSee.label: Trades are priced on one field
cannotSee.body: Only a full-season projection is published, and season-long value is the right unit for a trade. There is no way to price a trade on a rest-of-season market from this data.
